transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sasha Ivanov (Helios CTO), Priya Rao (Helios ML Eng), Mark Bennett (Infra)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Maya, AE on this account, and Diego is our SE. how's everyone's day?
[00:07] Sasha: Good, thanks. We wanted to focus on POC scope — specifically cost modeling, benchmark expectations, and timelines.
[00:12] Diego: Great. we'll walk through typical unit economics, batching/caching knobs, and then map that to your traffic profile. feel free to interrupt.
[00:20] Priya: sound good. we sent over a high-level traffic sheet but not the prompt set yet.
[00:23] Maya: perfect, that's fine. Mark, any infra constraints we should know about?
[00:27] Mark: yeah, we need VPC-only traffic, no egress to public endpoints for sensitive models. also strict IAM & KMS policies.
[00:33] Diego: ok noted — Private deployment or dedicated with VPC peering both possible. we'll call out what needs to be in the security review.

Summary & goals (spoken):
[00:40] Maya: Goal for POC: validate latency SLOs, measure per-token costs given your mix, and a baseline quality check on our chosen model. success criteria you gave earlier were sub-200ms median for short prompts and cost under $X per active user — let's nail that down.
[00:55] Sasha: right, ideally we want to see realistic monthly cost to budget planning. our initial IRR from the product team is target < $0.10/user/month for the conversational assistant.

Workload & sizing discussion:
[01:05] Priya: our expected steady state is ~50k requests/day, avg prompt+response ~150 tokens. Peak concurrency around 200 qps for short bursts.
[01:12] Diego: ok 50k/day * 150 tokens = 7.5M tokens/day ~225M tokens/month. that math checks out.
[01:20] Maya: to translate to dollars — sample hosted cost ballpark: for a mid-size open LLM variant we typically model $0.0005/token raw; so at that raw rate your unoptimized monthly bill would be ~112.5k.
[01:33] Sasha: whoa, that's higher than expected. can you break down where we can lower it?
[01:36] Diego: yes — three main levers: batching to reduce compute overhead, KV/prefix caching to avoid repeating tokens, and dedicated/reserved capacity which lowers per-token execution cost for high throughput.
[01:45] Priya: how realistic is caching? our users have many unique queries but a few repeated intents.
[01:50] Diego: in most assistants we see ~20-40% prefix reuse for system prompts and common intents; with smart prefix/KV caching you can see effective token reduction of ~25-35% for those flows. if your workload is more unique, caching benefit is lower.
[02:02] Mark: and batching? we don't want to add latency.
[02:05] Diego: Redwood supports dynamic batching; you can tune target latency vs batch size. for your peak profile we estimate 15-20% token cost reduction without increasing median latency beyond 20-30ms, but tail latency can be impacted if you over-batch.

Cost modeling examples (spoken + rough numbers):
[02:20] Maya: example scenarios:
[02:22] - Hosted baseline (no caching, minimal batching): 225M tokens/mo * $0.0005/token = $112,500/mo.
[02:28] - Hosted + batching (15% savings): ~$95,625/mo.
[02:33] - Hosted + batching + KV caching (30% additional): ~$66,937/mo.
[02:38] - Dedicated reserved pool (monthly commit + lower per-token): e.g., $40k/mo reserved + $0.00018/token * 225M = $40k + $40,500 = ~$80,500/mo; with batching/caching that can drop to ~$48k-$55k/mo depending on cache hit rate.
[02:50] Priya: ok that makes the dedicated proposition more interesting.

Benchmarks & metrics we want to run:
[03:00] Diego: we'll run three primary benchmark types: throughput (tokens/sec, requests/sec), latency tails (p50/p95/p99), and cost per 1k tokens computed from observed GPU utilization + instance amortization.
[03:10] Diego: for latency we'll target p95 < 250ms for your short prompt flows and median < 120ms. for throughput we'll validate steady state with your 200 qps bursts.
[03:20] Sasha: what environment will benchmarks run in?
[03:23] Maya: depends — we can do hosted runs against a Redwood test project, or we can run the same harness inside your VPC on Dedicated / Private. for security reasons you might prefer dedicated/private tests.
[03:33] Mark: we prefer VPC private testing. also need SOC2 docs.
[03:36] Maya: we'll share SOC2 and encryption/KMS docs.

Transcription glitch / mis-said terms (authenticity):
[03:45] Priya: can you explain K-V chase —
[03:47] Diego: K-V cache, sorry, kw- cache, it's the KV (key-value) cache for past tokens and prefixes. sometimes the auto-transcript writes K-V chase, ha.

POC timeline & milestones:
[04:00] Maya: propose a 4-week POC:
[04:03] - Week 0 (pre-work): security checklist, access, prompt set + traffic profile delivered by Helios
[04:08] - Week 1: infra setup (VPC peering or dedicated), baseline quick smoke tests
[04:12] - Week 2: full benchmark runs (throughput & latency), initial cost calc
[04:17] - Week 3: integration with your service, run representative traffic and caching scenarios
[04:21] - Week 4: evaluate results, finalize recommended configuration (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and next steps for rollout
[04:26] Sasha: that timeline looks good; product wants go/no-go decision at end of week 4.

Example benchmark config (spoken):
[04:35] Diego: we'll need: concurrency profile (arrival rates with bursts), sample prompts (you said ~1000 to start), expected response length distribution, and a few target SLOs (latency, availability). Darwin-ish numbers: run 30-minute steady runs + 5-10 minute spike runs to capture tail behavior.
[04:48] Priya: we'll bundle those up.

Edge cases & tradeoffs discussed:
[04:55] Maya: important tradeoff: aggressive batching reduces per-token cost but can increase tail latency. caching reduces tokens but only for repeated prefixes; model size/quantization affects cost/latency too. Diego: quantized model builds reduce GPU memory and cost but sometimes show slight quality deltas — we should include a quality check in POC.
[05:12] Sasha: we also care about regression detection — if accuracy drops after quantization, we need an eval suite.
[05:16] Diego: absolutely — we'll run an automatic eval on the sample prompts comparing baseline FP16 model vs int8/int4 variants.

Security & compliance notes spoken:
[05:25] Mark: need proof of key management separation, audit logs retention 12 months, and SSO/SAML integration.
[05:30] Maya: we'll send the compliance pack and a template for audit log retention and KMS flow.

Recap & next steps (spoken):
[05:38] Maya: recap — Redwood to send POC pricing sheet, benchmark harness, and security docs. Helios to share prompts, traffic profile, and confirm VPC constraints. schedule initial benchmark for week of April 6.
[05:49] Sasha: agreed. Priya will own prompt set, Mark will handle infra checks.
[05:53] Maya: great. we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark run and provide a step-by-step playbook.
[05:58] Diego: one more note — if you want, we can run a quick exploratory run on our hosted infra for speed, then replicate in your VPC to validate parity. helps catch config issues early.
[06:07] Priya: let's do that. thanks everyone.

Final timestamps re-confirmed: call ends ~15:52 UTC.

References mentioned in call: Redwood POC pricing spreadsheet (link), benchmark harness repo (link), SOC2 + KMS compliance pack (link).

Action items (spoken):
- Maya to send pricing and benchmark config by 2026-04-02.
- Diego to share perf test harness and example scripts by 2026-04-06.
- Helios (Priya) to share 1000 sample prompts by 2026-04-03.
- Helios (Mark) to confirm VPC firewall rules and peering details by 2026-04-05.

End of transcript.
